title: Quantitative Analysis Explained Simply | PUC Chemistry Class 11
description:
A food packet says how much protein is inside. In this animated lesson for Class 11 Chemistry (Chapter 8, Organic Chemistry: Some Basic Principles and Techniques) Diya wonders how anyone knows, and we learn how chemists find the percentage of each element in a compound.

You will see Liebig's method live on the molecule bench (CO2 trapped in KOH, water in anhydrous CaCl2) and derive %C = 12/44 and %H = 2/18 of the masses. Then nitrogen by Dumas (28 g in 22400 mL at STP) and Kjeldahl (and why it fails for nitro, azo and ring nitrogen), halogens by the Carius method (AgBr 188, Br 80), sulphur as BaSO4 (233), phosphorus as ammonium phosphomolybdate (1877) and oxygen by difference. A worked example, the 2/18 trap, an original JEE Main pattern question, a recap card and three questions to check yourself. For NCERT, CBSE, ICSE/ISC, PUC, NEET and JEE students.

This is Episode 88 of our PUC Chemistry series. 

Made for PUC (Karnataka), CBSE Class 11, NEET and JEE Main students.

In this video:

1:16 Deriving %C and %H
1:40 Nitrogen: Dumas and Kjeldahl
2:31 Carius: halogens, sulphur, phosphorus, oxygen
3:11 Dumas vs Kjeldahl, pause and think
3:42 Worked example: %C and %H
4:22 Exam trap: 2/18 for hydrogen
